## Discussion & Activity

Sit with the uncomfortable reflection: consider your morning routine — the coffee, the commute, the neighborhood — and then the homeless person you passed on the way here. How do our lifestyle choices — where we live, how we move, what we consume — contribute to the economic systems that produce homelessness? In what ways do our feelings of generosity when we give to church programs actually *insulate* us from confronting the impact of our daily decisions? How do we move beyond feeling good about occasional charity to choices that promote justice in everyday life? (The aim is participation, not guilt: we are naming ourselves as actors inside systems of justice or injustice, never mere observers — the Polygons lesson, now personal.)
